subject: Business
title: Logrolling: Trading What You Value Differently
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Logrolling: Trading What You Value Differently.

hook.text: You care about price. They care about delivery speed. You can give them fast delivery cheaply and get a lower price.

buildup.text: Logrolling means each side concedes on issues they value less in exchange for gains on issues they value more.

discovery.text: It only works when parties value issues differently — which is nearly always the case.

twist.text: Single-issue negotiations can't use logrolling. That's why expanding the agenda often helps both sides.

climax.text: Labor unions trade overtime rules for wage increases all the time. Both sides walk away feeling they won.

punchline.text: Trade what's cheap for you and expensive for them.

quiz.question: What is logrolling in negotiation?
options: Trading concessions on differently valued issues to benefit both sides
Rolling logs as a trust-building exercise

details.summary: Logrolling is the integrative negotiation technique of trading concessions on issues the parties value differently. By identifying where you care deeply and your counterpart does not, each side can give up low-cost items in exchange for high-value gains, creating mutual benefit.
details.whyItMatters: Logrolling transforms zero-sum standoffs into positive-sum trades. Most negotiations have multiple issues where the parties' priorities differ. Finding these asymmetries and trading across them is the single most reliable way to create value.
takeaways: Trade issues you value less for issues you value more in negotiation packages
Logrolling requires understanding what the other side prioritizes most
Multi-issue negotiations have more logrolling opportunities than single-issue ones

faq.question: How do you identify logrolling opportunities in a negotiation?
faq.answer: Ask open-ended questions about the other side's priorities and constraints. Share your own priorities honestly. Look for issues where you are flexible and they are not, and vice versa. Negotiate multiple issues simultaneously as packages rather than resolving one issue at a time.

faq.question: What is a concrete example of logrolling?
faq.answer: In a job negotiation, the employer might value keeping the salary at a specific level while the candidate values remote work flexibility. Trading a lower salary for remote work days costs the employer nothing but is highly valued by the candidate. Both sides gain from the trade.
